title: Smooth observation may remove discontinuities without removing scale dependence
problem: Test whether replacing R12's hard collision cutoff with a smooth Gaussian weight eliminates the critical-resolution scale phase.
failure: A smooth response does not imply a single critical scaling limit. R13 provides a counterexample to that possible inference, not a failed physical experiment.
correction: Reindex the parity lattice by its Pell-unit automorphism and use the local limit theorem with Gaussian domination. Certify nonconstancy of the analytic periodic limiting function by exact rational bounds at two phases, including a tail estimate.
transfer: When changing an observation model, separate discontinuity artifacts from structural scale dependence. Test the latter after smoothing, and certify small differences against truncation and rounding errors.
limits: One Gaussian response in the regular unit octagonal walk. R13 proves an analytic periodic phase profile and a gap greater than 0.03 between two phases. No minimal-period or global-extremum claim, no finite-time Gaussian path simulation, no independent review or physical inference.
